messages:
Jessica (Support): escalating from ticket #4237 — ACME (Bob) reports model outputs started returning stale/mismatched content after last night's rollout (deploy 2026-03-12 02:05 UTC). Customer says summaries are pulling other tenants' data or previous convo snippets. They consider this a P1 for live billing/job flows.

Bob (ACME): quick repro below. We call /v1/generate with the same prompt and sometimes get account details from another customer. First seen ~02:10 UTC. Request ids: req_8f3c, req_8f5a. Repro:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -H 'X-Tenant-ID: acme-corp' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-2026","input":"Summarize latest invoice for account ACME"}'
```Response (unexpected): includes phrase "ACME-Partner LLC" which is not in ACME's data.

Lena (Support): thanks Bob — adding eng. Did you notice if it only affects summaries or also chat completions/edits?

Bob (ACME): mostly summarize/structured outputs where we rely on prefixing customer data. Chat streams also had a few bad tokens.

Marc (eng-runtime): looking at logs for the req ids. Filing initial hypothesis: prefix/KV cache keying regressed in the perf patch merged yesterday (runtime PR #4128). It appears tenant_id was inadvertently dropped when building the prefix cache key for short prefixes which means the same cache entry can be reused across tenants. :grimacing:

Marc (eng-runtime): relevant log snippet:```
[2026-03-12T02:10:23Z] GET_KV_CACHE key=prefix_hash:0x7a3b model=redwood-large-2026 user=unknown -> hit
[2026-03-12T02:10:23Z] APPLY_KV_CACHE kv_entries=12 tenant_id=
```Notice tenant_id is blank for some hits.

Anya (eng-ml): that would explain content leakage between prompt prefixes. The new continuous-prefix cache was trying to normalize hashes and we scoped down keys to speed lookups; if tenant scoping got removed, different tenant prefixes can collide. It won't always trigger — depends on hash collisions + same model_version + prefix length.

Marc (eng-runtime): quick repro locally by forcing the same prefix_hash across two tenant ids:```bash
# emulate two tenants hitting same prefix hash
echo '{"tenant":"acme","prefix":"Invoice: ACME"}' > /tmp/a.json
echo '{"tenant":"other","prefix":"Invoice: ACME"}' > /tmp/b.json
# run the cache-store util (local dev)
./bin/cache-store --file /tmp/a.json --model redwood-large-2026
./bin/cache-store --file /tmp/b.json --model redwood-large-2026
# then fetch for acme -> returns entries that include other tenant's ids
./bin/cache-fetch --tenant acme --model redwood-large-2026 --prefix-hash 0x7a3b
```Observed: fetch returns a block containing tokens that reference `other_corp_id`.

Oliver (eng-sre): temporary mitigations: 1) disable prefix caching for the ACME tenant via per-tenant flag in config service, 2) roll back the canary, 3) apply immediate patch to restore tenant scoping in key. Recommend disabling prefix cache for affected customers while we patch.

Lena (Support): I've initiated a per-tenant toggle for acme-corp (DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true) and notified Bob. Also offered to rollback the deploy if needed. Bob — would disabling prefix cache be an acceptable short-term fix?

Bob (ACME): yes please disable it, anything to stop leakage. We're paused on a few jobs.

Marc (eng-runtime): created branch fix/cache-tenant-key — change is to include tenant_id and model_version in cache key + stricter prefix length sampling. Small diff:```diff
- key = f"prefix:{prefix_hash}"
+ key = f"prefix:{model_version}:{tenant_id}:{prefix_hash}"
```Will run unit + integration and request canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started by marc — rollout id r-2026-03-12-4128-canary, canary=10% (5 instances), region=us-west-2.

Sarah (product): were there canary alerts we missed? We saw perf numbers improve but not correctness signals. Can we add an eval that asserts tenant isolation for prefix cache?

Anya (eng-ml): yes, adding a synthetic eval that runs cross-tenant prefix collisions and asserts no cross-tenant exposures. I'll push an integration test to the evals harness.

Marc (eng-runtime): canary looks clean so far, 02:40 UTC 5 instances. Real-time logs show tenant_id present in key now. Requesting gradual rollout.

Oliver (eng-sre): please also invalidate prefix cache entries now to remove any stale entries that were cross-tenant. Command:```bash
# invalidate matching prefix hashes in Redis
redis-cli -h cache.internal 'KEYS' 'prefix_hash:*' | xargs -r redis-cli -h cache.internal DEL
```Note: this is blunt — will flush many keys. Prefer using a targeted script to delete only entries without tenant scoping if we have metadata.

Marc (eng-runtime): pushed targeted invalidation script that scans keys missing tenant_id tag and deletes them. Running now.

Lena (Support): Bob confirms they no longer see cross-tenant phrases after we toggled the flag and after the canary patch. Bob: "looks good on our side, no wrong account names in recent runs." :thumbsup:

Bob (ACME): thanks everyone — appreciate fast turnaround. Please confirm root cause and follow-up actions.

Marc (eng-runtime): root cause: regression in prefix cache key generation from PR #4128 where tenant scoping was accidentally removed for certain short-prefix codepath. Fix: include tenant_id+model_version in key and add unit test. Follow-ups: 1) add cross-tenant isolation eval to CI, 2) add per-tenant toggles as emergency kill-switch (done), 3) add telemetry that tracks tenant_id presence for cache hits.

Sarah (product): will update postmortem template and add a checklist to include correctness evals for cache-related perf changes.

deploy-bot: rollout r-2026-03-12-4128 completed to 100% at 03:12 UTC (stable).

Oliver (eng-sre): closing incident after monitoring window (2h) — no regression signals in logs and affected customers confirmed.

Lena (Support): I'll update the ticket (4237) with notes and link to runtime PR #4132 and the rollback/toggle steps.

Jessica (Support): great teamwork. Marking this resolved for now — keep an eye for related tickets. :eyes:

Bob (ACME): confirmed resolved at 04:05 UTC, thanks all! :white_check_mark:
